checks: The only changes to the exact candidate are the properness qualification in the statement and its justification in the proof. Source provenance and the empty dependency list are unchanged.

For every fixed gamma>0, 1/m+exp(-2 gamma m) tends to zero and exp(-2 gamma m)>0, so the cut threshold is strictly between a and 1 for all sufficiently large m. The original counterexample at m=2 is outside this properness claim.

On that tail the omitted collar has normalized inverse mass at most (a+eta^2)log(1+eta)/(M_m c_m), tending to zero. Its cut coarea is a+eta^2, and multiplying by gamma m-log c_m-log(1+eta) tends to gamma because m eta^2 tends to zero. The rate tends to R, and the cut excludes the lower-edge exterior atom.

Deleting finitely many indices preserves the common weak limit. The full inverse and exterior defect calculations, inside-support and complementary allocations, and diagonal half-incidence calculation retain their exact hypotheses and constants.
The source hashes match the pinned original candidates. The revised and original statement and proof field hashes are computed from their decoded UTF-8 values.

The (t,q) Jacobian is t and M_m=(1-a^2)/2. With v=t-a+eta, direct integration gives Z_m=1-a+(a-eta)log((1-a+eta)/eta) and the first t moment numerator M_m+(a-eta)Z_m. Thus c_m tends to exp(1/2), Z_m tends to 1+gamma, the stated centroid coordinates are correct, and the tilted row divided by its marked L value is exactly the normalized inverse-volume measure.
The limiting source coordinates are positive and their sum is strictly below 1; comparison against the four facet inequalities gives a uniform own inball and a positive limiting marked value.

Splitting t/v=1+(a-eta)/v isolates the defect. The latter spatial mass is concentrated near the origin, and the rate Jacobian gamma m/R and normalization by M_m c_m yield density 2 gamma/(cR) on the limiting rate interval. The zero-rate part of that term has vanishing mass; the first term has no atom at the origin.

The lower edge has length sqrt(2)/m and logarithm gamma m-log c_m, giving surface mass sqrt(2) gamma and limiting rate R. The two coordinate edges have logarithmic integrals over v in a shrinking interval at the origin, so contribute no additional atom.

The inside lower support has coarea a, since its edge length is sqrt(2)a and the normal length is sqrt(2). For sufficiently large m the offset cut is proper; its discarded inverse collar is bounded by a constant times (a+eta^2)log(1+eta), and its section mass tends to gamma. Complementary allocations add in body and volume and share the same section term.

At x=y the diagonal cut halves each transverse inverse slice and the lower-edge log measure. Along the section coarea is dt/2 and the local log is uniformly integrable near the origin, yielding zero section defect despite half of each other defect at the closed-cap incidence point.

Original 91145d6ea212266a §§6–7 gives the two cap calibrations; 1b1d5e313c1943d1 §§1–4 verifies the unlifted one-row calibration at gamma=log 2. The frozen proof supplies the extension to any gamma>0 and the rate-resolved claims.
